title: Appraisal & Spatial Modeling Methodology
text:
The RailActive appraisal framework integrates spatial network analysis with empirical demand modeling and the UK Department for Transport’s (DfT) Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT) to evaluate the economic, health, and environmental case for corridor interventions.
The workflow comprises three interlinked analytical stages:

Spatial Network Categorisation: Ingestion and classification of civil engineering haul roads, access tracks, and intersecting rights of way.
Empirical Demand Segmentation: Calibrating baseline active travel uptake across utility (commuting, education, shopping) and leisure purposes using the National Travel Survey (NTS) and Active Lives Survey (ALS).
Multi-Modal Economic Appraisal: Quantifying 15 appraisal components across health, economy, environment, and capital costs following official TAG guidance.

title: Appraisal & Spatial Modeling Methodology
text:
2 Travel Demand & Trip Purpose Modeling
Traditional transport appraisal tools frequently focus solely on the commute-to-work (e.g. Census Journey to Work matrices or the Propensity to Cycle Tool). For a national or regional spine route like the HS2 corridor, this introduces a severe undercounting risk.

2.1 Empirical Insights from National Datasets
Analysis of recent microdata from the UK Data Service reveals the true distribution of active travel in England:

National Travel Survey (NTS, 2022–2024):

Leisure Cycling (39.7%): The single largest purpose for cycling, outstripping commuting (29.9%).
Leisure Walking (57.9%): Walking for leisure or exercise (“just walk”) accounts for 42.5% of walking trips, whereas commuting walking represents only 6.7%.
Trip Distance & Duration: Leisure cycle trips average 4.20 miles (6.76 km) and 29.9 minutes, compared to 3.43 miles (5.52 km) and 22.9 minutes for commuting. Leisure cyclists spend 31% more time per journey exercising.

Sport England Active Lives Survey (ALS, Year 9, 2023–2024):

Participation: 31.9% of adults cycle for leisure and sport annually, compared to 11.3% for travel.
Activity Volume: Leisure accounts for 70.5% of total cycling minutes and 61.5% of total walking minutes across the population.


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             Active Mode Demand Composition             │
├─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
│ Cycling Trips (NTS)     │ 39.7% Leisure | 29.9% Work   │
│ Cycling Time (ALS)      │ 70.5% Leisure | 29.5% Travel │
│ Walking Trips (NTS)     │ 57.9% Leisure |  6.7% Work   │
└─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘

title: Appraisal & Spatial Modeling Methodology
text:
3 Economic Benefits Appraisal (DfT AMAT)
Economic benefits are evaluated using a concise, verified base-R implementation of AMAT (railactive/amat).

3.1 Appraisal Components

Premature Death Reduction (Health):

Uses the WHO Health Economic Assessment Tool (HEAT) dose-response curve adapted for TAG:

\[\text{RR} = \max\left(0.55, \exp\left(\frac{\ln(0.90)}{11.25} \times \text{MET-hours/week}\right)\right)\]

Attributable deaths avoided are calculated across 5 age bands for males and females and valued using discounted Years of Life Lost (YLL) at £92,240 per life-year.

Workplace Absenteeism:

Sickness absence reduction (0.25 days per user per year) applied to employed new users, valued at average regional daily labor output (£267.36/day).

Journey Ambience & Quality:

Valued using the Rule of a Half for existing users and new switchers:

\[\text{Benefit} = \left(\text{Trips}_{\text{existing}} + \frac{\text{Trips}_{\text{new}}}{2}\right) \times \Delta\text{Rate} \times \text{Time on Scheme} \times \text{VoT}_{\text{non-work}}\]

Upgrading from “No provision” to “Off-road segregated cycle track” yields an amenity improvement of 16.28 pence per minute.

Decongestion & Environmental Externalities:

Mode-shift from private cars and taxis reduces vehicle-kilometres:

\[\text{Vehicle-km Reduced} = \text{Trips}_{\text{new}} \times \text{Trip Length} \times \text{Days} \times \left(\frac{\text{Car Divert}}{\text{Car Occupancy}} + \frac{\text{Taxi Divert}}{\text{Taxi Occupancy}}\right)\]

Savings are calculated across 7 marginal external cost streams: highway congestion, infrastructure wear, collision risk, local air quality (\(PM_{2.5}\), \(NO_x\)), ambient noise, greenhouse gas emissions (\(CO_2e\)), and indirect taxation losses.

title: Data and Documentation Inventory
text:
This document catalogs incoming data assets received in the October 2026 project archive (OneDrive_2026-10-05.zip).
The archive comprises 42 primary assets (~623 MB uncompressed) plus 3 nested spatial archives containing over 280 shapefiles and KMZ layers. These assets span strategic policy and benefits reviews, engineering feasibility studies by John Grimshaw CBE, site access road (SAR) retention proposals, public rights of way (PRoW), canals, local cycling plans (LCWIPs), and economic appraisal models using the DfT Active Modes Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT).

title: Data and Documentation Inventory
text:
4 Thematic Cluster Profiles

4.1 Cluster 1: Spatial Network & Core GIS Layers (WP2)

Corridor Alignments: Official shapefiles and KML representations of the North-South active travel corridor across Phase 1, Phase 2a, and regional feeder branches.
Public Rights of Way & Local Networks: Over 280 spatial layers spanning definitive PRoW maps (Buckinghamshire, Northamptonshire, Staffordshire, Warwickshire), Canal & River Trust (CRT) waterways, Crewe and Warwickshire LCWIP priority networks, and the TfWM Starley Network.



4.2 Cluster 2: John Grimshaw Engineering & Feasibility Studies (WP1 / WP2)

All-Sections Design Notes (HS2-DFT-HW-REP-000-000002, 309.4 MB): Detailed engineering notes documenting civil works interfaces along Phase 1 and Phase 2a, identifying overbridges, underpasses, trace crossings, and potential greenway alignments.
HS2 Cycleway Feasibility Report (HS2-DFT-HW-REP-000-000002, 14.7 MB): Baseline feasibility study establishing how a continuous national cycling and walking corridor can be achieved alongside railway civil engineering works.
County-Level Interface Studies: Granular interface assessments for Buckinghamshire, Northamptonshire, Warwickshire, Solihull, Birmingham, and Staffordshire.



4.3 Cluster 3: Section Infrastructure & Haul Road Retentions (WP2)

Wormleighton to Southam (Northamptonshire to Warwickshire): Specific engineering proposals to retain Site Access Roads (SAR), Construction Access Roads (CAR), and Maintenance Access Tracks (MAT) as permanent active travel infrastructure rather than removing them post-construction.
Buckinghamshire: Quainton to Calvert greenway alignment integrating with East West Rail (EWR) corridor connections.
West Midlands / Solihull: Engineering drawings and regional network integration connecting Birmingham Curzon Street, Birmingham Interchange, and Coventry.



4.4 Cluster 4: Economic Appraisal (AMAT) & Demand Evidence (WP3)

Rural Schemes Economic Case Benchmark: Peer-reviewed strategic business cases establishing baseline benefit-cost ratios (BCRs) and monetised health/decongestion benefits for rural active travel schemes.
Route Case (RC) Summaries: Granular scheme appraisal notes for key corridor sections: Balsall Common, Ladbroke, Old Oak Common, Wormleighton, and Amersham to Chalfont St Giles.
Empirical Baseline Count Data: Automatic counter counts from comparable greenway schemes to calibrate AMAT induced trip forecasts.



4.5 Cluster 5: Cost Benchmarks & Maintenance (WP3)

All-Sections Combined Cost Estimate (23105_HS2 Cost Estimate RevC.xlsx, 1.3 MB): Detailed itemized bill of quantities across all route sections, providing civil engineering, surfacing, drainage, structure, and fencing unit costs.
DfT Typical Costings Guide: DfT standard per-kilometer cost benchmarks for ambitious cycling schemes.
Sustrans Maintenance & Whole-Life Unit Costs: Annual operating and maintenance expenditure benchmarks (£/km/year) and 20-/30-year whole-life replacement cost models across surfacing options.

6 Priority Meeting Discussion Topics
For upcoming stakeholder and team meetings, the following priority agenda items are highlighted:

1. Haul Road / SAR Retention Window: Engage HS2 Ltd and main works civils contractors (MWCC) regarding contractor handover timetables for Site Access Roads in Warwickshire and Buckinghamshire before compound demobilization.
2. Alignment Harmonization: Agree on whether the Shapefile (North-South Cycleway Alignment.zip) or the KML (Copy of North - South Cycleway 2025.kml) is adopted as the definitive v2026 centerline for the pipeline and web map.
3. AMAT Appraisal Scenarios: Confirm whether economic appraisal will be reported as a unified whole-route corridor scheme (London to Birmingham) or modular route cases (e.g. Balsall Common, Ladbroke, Quainton-Calvert, Old Oak Common).
4. Data Sharing & Licensing Protocol: Establish which layers can be published openly on the public web map (e.g. PRoW, NCN, LCWIPs, corridor centerline) vs proprietary HS2 contractor drawings that remain internal to the project team.

title: RailActive Data Dictionary & Dataset Register
text:
This document defines the machine-readable data dictionary and datasets register for the RailActive project and application.
The register standardizes data structures, variable names, units, and licensing across active datasets (North-South Corridor, custom GPX re-alignments, OS OpenRoads, DfT STATS19 road safety, OpenStreetMap active travel infrastructure, and the National Cycle Network), while tracking dependencies for forthcoming datasets (trip attractors, LCWIPs, OSMRN/PSGA, and OS NGD pavements).
Underlying schemas are version-controlled and available for download:

data/datasets_overview.csv: High-level dataset catalog and status
data/data_dictionary.csv: Full variable schema and technical definitions
data/data_dictionary.json: Web-ready JSON format consumed by the frontend

title: RailActive Data Dictionary & Dataset Register
text:
4 Forthcoming & TBC Datasets
The following candidate datasets are currently under scoping or awaiting licensing approval and data delivery:

Trip Attractors (Schools & Strategic Developments): Primary and secondary schools (Get Information About Schools / GIAS) and allocated residential and commercial sites within the 5 km study area to model first- and last-mile demand.
Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plans (LCWIPs): Spatial integration of adopted LCWIP networks from local transport authorities intersecting the corridor to ensure proposed HS2 infrastructure acts as a backbone for local feeder networks.
OS MasterMap Road Network (OSMRN / PSGA): Detailed carriageway widths, average traffic speeds, and vehicle access restrictions from Ordnance Survey under the Public Sector Geospatial Agreement.
Pavements & Footways in OS NGD: Dedicated pedestrian pavement geometry, effective footway widths, and severance barriers from the OS National Geographic Database.

title: RailActive Project Documentation
text:
RailActive investigates the potential to repurpose High Speed Two (HS2) construction assets—including haul roads, access tracks, and maintenance strips—into a high-quality, segregated, multi-user active travel spine.
The corridor stretches from London Euston / Old Oak Common through the Colne Valley, Chilterns, and rural Midlands into Birmingham Curzon Street, with wider strategic feeder links extending toward the North West.
Key project aims include:

Infrastructure Repurposing: Identifying where temporary construction access roads and haul tracks can be permanently retained for cycling, walking, and wheeling.
Severance Reduction: Overcoming historical and modern transport barriers (motorways, rail corridors, rivers) to reconnect fragmented rural communities.
Empirical Demand Modeling: Integrating commute, school, and leisure trip generators to estimate uptake.
Economic Benefits Appraisal: Applying the Department for Transport’s (DfT) Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT) to quantify decongestion, health mortality, workplace absenteeism, and journey ambience benefits.

2 System Architecture
The RailActive analytical and web mapping platform uses a modern, cloud-native architecture combining R spatial pipelines with a serverless web frontend:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             Data Ingestion & Spatial Backend           │
│   R targets Pipeline (sf, dodgr, osmextract) + Python  │
│   Ingests: OSM, NCN, OS OpenRoads, HS2 Haul Routes,    │
│            DfT STATS19 Collisions, Census & NTS Data   │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Analytical Artifacts                 │
│         • GeoJSON / GeoParquet (spatial features)      │
│         • DuckDB Database (high-speed SQL queries)     │
│         • PMTiles (serverless vector map tiles)        │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Frontend Web Application             │
│    Svelte 5 (Runes) + MapLibre GL + DuckDB-WASM        │
│    Fast, client-side SQL querying and interactive map  │
│    rendering without requiring a live backend server   │
